s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with fever and vomiting
salient_findings: Rigid abdomen with diffuse severe tenderness
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on abdominal radiograph
Hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
key_facts: Soft stool without blood on digital rectal examination
Normal hemoglobin, white-cell and platelet counts
Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on abdominal radiograph
Dilated large-bowel loops on abdominal radiograph
5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region on ultrasonography
Hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops on ultrasonography, consistent with intussusception

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rigid abdomen, diffuse severe tenderness, and elevated C-reactive protein, which are common findings in acute appendicitis

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT, which could represent an inflamed Meckel's diverticulum

shortlist.label: Small bowel obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Air–fluid levels in the small bowel on abdominal radiograph, which is a common finding in small bowel obstruction

shortlist.label: Peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse severe tenderness and elevated C-reactive protein, which can be seen in peritonitis

raw.rationale: The presence of a 5-cm hyperechoic mass in the hypogastric region surrounded by intestinal loops on ultrasonography and a hyperdense midline mass above the bladder on non-contrast abdominal CT, along with symptoms of abdominal pain, vomiting, and constipation, are highly suggestive of intussusception, which is a condition where a part of the intestine telescopes into another part.

rejected.label: Acute appendicitis
rejected.why: While acute appendicitis can cause abdominal pain and fever, the presence of a mass in the hypogastric region and the specific radiographic findings are more consistent with intussusception.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulitis
rejected.why: Meckel's diverticulitis typically presents with pain and inflammation in the right lower quadrant, which is not consistent with the midline mass seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Small bowel obstruction
rejected.why: While small bowel obstruction can cause abdominal pain and vomiting, the presence of a discrete mass on imaging studies is more suggestive of intussusception.

rejected.label: Peritonitis
rejected.why: Peritonitis is a more diffuse process that can cause abdominal pain and tenderness, but the specific findings of a mass in the hypogastric region and air-fluid levels in the small bowel are more consistent with intussusception.
